name: ask_human
title: Ask a human
description: Ask a human for a decision or information you cannot find or decide yourself. The answer arrives later as a team message: do not wait or poll; continue with independent work or end your turn. The team's coordinating member screens it first (within 10 minutes) and tells you what became of it.

question.description: One clear question. The answerer is usually no specialist and often on a phone: name the decision in one plain sentence in everyday words, then only the context needed to choose. Never ask for an approval label: an answer sets none, the app asks the label holders itself.

options.description: Suggested answers shown as buttons: a short label and its consequence (a plain label string is accepted too). Required for a decision, a yes/no question too; omit only with response_purpose information. The answerer can always write another answer.

consequence.description: What happens if the human picks this option, in everyday words.

recommended.description: The label of the option you recommend, written exactly the same way. Always give it, with recommendation_reason.

recommendation_reason.description: Why you recommend it, in one plain sentence. Needs recommended.

details.description: Code, file names and technical reasoning as markdown, shown folded: the question must make sense without it.

task_key.description: Task the question is about. Defaults to the task of your current session.

to.description: Handles of the humans to ask. Omit to ask the humans responsible for the task or project.

attachments.description: Ids (att_…) of the files, on the question's card or its parent (list_attachments), the human needs to look at to answer, instead of describing where to find them. At most 6.

reask_of.description: Only when the team's coordinating member answered, forwarded or closed your earlier question and you still need a person's answer: its id. The new one goes to the people unscreened; needs reask_reason.

reask_reason.description: Why a person must see it after all. Needs reask_of.

signal_id.description: Only the project manager: the open system signal delivered to you that this question is about; always give it for a question about a signal. The question closes by itself when the signal's case ends; task_key defaults to the signal's card. Refused (signal_not_for_owner) for an unreleased, structural_pattern, milestone_closed and review_follow_ups signal: the owners are not asked about those.

recipient.description: Suggested todo recipient; it does not decide. Screening sends a todo to the integrator whenever one can take it, to the owner only when none can or the question is protected. When screening is skipped, `integrator` stays the recipient as a todo; any other question waits for the project manager.

response_purpose.description: information: a plain factual question, no decision; the integrator may relay the answer; needs no options. owner_decision (default): a choice or anything with cost, deletion or security; only the owner answers.

owner_topic.description: Only the project manager's own decision question, a re-ask, or a question nobody screens: the id of the project's owner topic it falls under (role guide); refused without one (owner_topic_required).
